subject: math

objective.text: Measure one object with two different length units and compare. See how the size of the unit changes the number.

explanations.title: Same object, two units
explanations.text: Measure one pencil with an inch ruler and a centimeter ruler. You get two different numbers. Both are correct. The units are different.

explanations.title: Smaller unit, more units
explanations.text: A centimeter is smaller than an inch. It takes more centimeters to cover the same length. The smaller the unit, the more units you need.

explanations.title: Bigger unit, fewer units
explanations.text: An inch is bigger than a centimeter. The bigger the unit, the fewer units you use.

explanations.title: 5 inches and 5 centimeters
explanations.text: Draw a line 5 inches long and a line 5 centimeters long. The 5-inch line is longer. One inch is longer than one centimeter.

explanations.title: Use what you know
explanations.text: 13 centimeters is about 5 inches. A line with more than 13 centimeters is longer than 5 inches. You do not have to measure again.

explanations.title: Break apart 20 inches
explanations.text: A decomposition tree breaks a whole into two parts. The two parts add up to the whole. You can break 20 inches in many ways.

examples.title: The pencil
examples.text: The pencil is about 7 inches long. It is about 18 centimeters long. Both are correct. We need more centimeters because they are smaller.

examples.title: Thomas and Chris
examples.text: Thomas says the crayon is 8 centimeters. Chris says it is 3 inches. Both are right. They used different units.

questions.text: Break 20 inches into two parts. Name one pair of parts.
Break 20 inches into two parts. One part is 12 inches. What is the other part?
Break 20 inches into two parts. One part is 5 inches. What is the other part?
Ezra thinks his bed is about 2 yards long. Is this a reasonable estimate? Why?
You measure a pencil with an inch ruler and with a centimeter ruler. Are both measurements correct?
Which is longer, one centimeter or one inch?
The pencil is about 7 inches or about 18 centimeters. Did you use more inches or more centimeters?
Why do you need more centimeters than inches to measure the pencil?
Does the length of the pencil change when you use a different unit?
When the unit is smaller, do you need more of that unit or fewer?
When the unit is bigger, do you need more of that unit or fewer?
Which line is longer, a 5-inch line or a 5-centimeter line?
About how many centimeters are the same length as 5 inches?
About how many inches are the same length as 5 centimeters?
A line is 15 centimeters long. Is it longer or shorter than 5 inches?
Thomas measures a crayon and says 8 centimeters. Chris says 3 inches. Why can both be correct?
Takeesha draws a line 9 centimeters long. Damani draws a line 4 inches long. Whose line is longer?
Takeesha says her line is longer because 9 is greater than 4. Why might she be wrong?
Why is it important to label a length with the unit?
What word do we use for a measurement that is not exact?
Why does the size of the unit matter when we measure?
When would you measure with a small unit? When would you use a large unit?
